Subject: APAC zone isolation — immediate traffic reroute, opt-in & follow-up

Hi Ava —

Quick note to say we observed an isolation event affecting one APAC availability zone starting ~15:40 UTC. The platform automatically triggered our regional fallback to the nearest healthy APAC pool for affected tenants; for most traffic that means transparent reroute with minimal retrying.

What we need from you (short list):
- Opt-in to extended reroute window (we'll keep traffic off the impacted zone for up to 72h while infra completes a controlled remediation). Opt-in form attached (medsync-opt-in-form.csv) or reply OK and I’ll file it for you.
- Confirm whether you want us to enable the sidecar-by-default for your tenant (reduces tokenization latency during the reroute). If you’re unsure, say "sidecar: enable" and I’ll coordinate.

Impact right now:~
- Estimated 4–12% of requests saw increased latency or transient 502s during the initial failover window (our telemetry).
- We have throttled bursty background jobs automatically; no change to authentication or data residency.

We’re standing up a short 30-minute bridge at 17:00 PST for any customers who want a walkthrough; I’ll send the invite separately. I’ll keep you updated with a concise post-incident note once remediation completes.

Attachments: apac-reroute-playbook-v1.pdf, medsync-opt-in-form.csv

Apologies for the disruption — we’re prioritizing stability for production traffic.

— Naomi

Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 10:32:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — APAC zone isolation (Feb 20)

Ava — thanks again for confirming the opt-in and for enabling sidecar. Below is a short, customer-facing post-incident summary and next steps. If anything looks wrong, flag it and I’ll revise.

Incident summary (timeline):
- 15:40 UTC (Feb 20): SierraCloud reported control-plane instability in ap-east-1 causing the zone to isolate from the regional mesh.
- 15:41–15:50 UTC: Redwood automatic fallback routed traffic to nearest healthy APAC pools; a portion of requests retried and experienced transient 502s or increased tail latency while KV caches warmed. Impact window for MedSync estimated at ~8% of requests.
- 16:05 UTC: Customer communications outbound (this thread).
- 16:45 UTC: MedSync opt-in received; sidecar-by-default enabled for tenant 3482.
- 17:10 UTC: Finance approved a one-time 10% usage credit for February; credit will appear on next invoice.

What we did:
- Triggered automatic fallback (no customer config changes required).
- Enabled sidecar-by-default for MedSync to reduce tokenization delays during redirected traffic.
- Engaged SierraCloud ops and our infra team to validate routing convergence and KV cache rehydration.

Customer action items:
- Validate traffic to your APAC endpoints for the next 72h and confirm if you want us to keep the extended reroute beyond that window. Reply "keep-reroute" or "revert".
- If you see any residual errors, include request IDs and timestamps — we’ll correlate against our trace logs.

Attachments: apac-reroute-playbook-v1.pdf (walkthrough of how we reroute + optional sidecar config), medsync-opt-in-form.csv, credit-draft-approval.txt

If you’d like a deeper postmortem or an exec-brief for your leadership, I can schedule one this week with our reliability leads.

Thanks for your patience, and sorry again for the disruption.

— Naomi
